### Risks

- Do not turn acceptance clauses into individual tests or reopen the historical Explorer qualification campaign.
- A newly observed failure justifies its own narrow correction/recheck, not unrelated suite expansion.

### Acceptance criteria

- The same build presents a distinct synthetic project identity/purpose with no ontology snapshot or live depot dependency, without repeating the full main browser journey.
- Neutral starter and custom-copy/rerun preservation are evidenced with the smallest applicable fixture; shared owner coverage is referenced rather than duplicated.
- Each added or rerun focused check states its uncovered changed risk, such as source revocation, safe rendering, stale responses, owned shutdown or executable-mode/adoption handling; unchanged controls reuse applicable evidence.
- No voice/screen-reader/certification, compatibility matrix, benchmark/stress, native-agent pilot or exhaustive optional-feature campaign is run.

### Planned verification

- Review TASK-001 evidence reuse against the final diff; run only selected focused cases for remaining changed risks and the bounded alternate configuration/preservation fixture. Record exact selectors and why each was necessary.

### Risks

- Browser evidence must come from actual interaction; screenshots or a child completion message alone do not establish unobserved flow success.
- If a required flow is blocked, record its exact limitation and perform only the necessary targeted follow-up.

### Acceptance criteria

- Actual launch opens the correct Home without a typed command, reopen targets its owned service, navigation/history and representative permitted content/source links work, and required controls are understandable.
- Relationship text remains usable without reliance on the graph; Lessons and decisions and any unavailable adapters are truthfully labeled.
- Closing a reading session and stopping the owned app show their real effects, retained existing Explorer access is checked concisely, and only documented transient state changes.
- The result records actual host/browser/package, observed steps and exact limitations, with no unsupported certification or broad runtime claim.

### Planned verification

- Execute this single combined smoke journey and compare protected governed-record hashes before/after; reuse its observations across all mapped requirements without repeating passed steps.

### Risks

- Keep product copy free of internal implementation detail unless it helps a reader decide what to do.
- Document changes affecting build identity require the normal explicit package refresh before recording final matching evidence; avoid changing build-owned prose after the final build.

### Acceptance criteria

- Every REQ-001 through REQ-031 maps to delivered artifacts and sufficient current evidence, or an explicit unresolved failure that prevents a false completion claim; every changed artifact has a requirement basis.
- Instructions describe real supported commands and the reviewed build; reusable source, neutral Template, root adoption and synthetic existing-project support are reported separately.
- Final inspection follows current evidence and affirmatively records each protected-path preservation result, current registry, plan/Task state separation and exact implementation limits.
- No Git/publication/deployment, unselected real-product adoption, cross-platform claim or historical full-release completion is inferred; stop after the scoped criteria are met.

### Planned verification

- Review final documents/links and final diff, compare protected manifests, and audit the source-to-requirement-to-task/evidence mappings; reuse current build, focused and browser results without another test campaign.
